aggregation_schema.inconsistency_policy: Preserve every raw repetition and aggregate as INCONSISTENT; never majority-vote disagreement away.

authority_exposure_outcomes.AUTHORITATIVE_AND_NONAUTHORITATIVE: All visible correlated records have direct evidence and both experiment authority classes are exposed.
authority_exposure_outcomes.AUTHORITATIVE_ONLY: All visible correlated records are attributable only to currently authoritative logical facts.
authority_exposure_outcomes.NONAUTHORITATIVE_ONLY: All visible correlated records are attributable only to non-authoritative logical facts.
authority_exposure_outcomes.NONE: No correlated retrieval record is observed.
authority_exposure_outcomes.UNKNOWN_PROVENANCE: At least one visible record cannot be directly attributed to an experiment source authority class.

content_hash_policy: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 content/context bytes

defense_conditions.D0: Provider/default retrieval with no authority filtering; only safety serialization or sanitization is permitted.
defense_conditions.D1: Pre-LLM enforcement may use directly visible lifecycle status or direct conflict state, but not inferred provenance.
defense_conditions.D2: Pre-LLM enforcement may use lifecycle authority plus directly observed provenance or lineage; no LLM judge is a security boundary.

exact_visibility_outcomes.ABSENT: Neither expected current nor stale exact string is observed in a valid retrieval.
exact_visibility_outcomes.CURRENT_AND_STALE: At least one expected current and one expected stale exact string are observed.
exact_visibility_outcomes.CURRENT_ONLY: At least one expected current exact string and no expected stale exact string are observed.
exact_visibility_outcomes.ERROR: The provider or harness operation unexpectedly failed.
exact_visibility_outcomes.STALE_ONLY: At least one expected stale exact string and no expected current exact string are observed.
exact_visibility_outcomes.UNSUPPORTED: The provider lacks the required native operation.

post_freeze_mutation_policy: After Phase 06B begins, Freeze v1 is immutable except typo-only documentation fixes; semantic changes require Experiment Freeze v2.

providers.name: Mem0
providers.quiescence: Native storage operations are synchronous; proceed only after the adapter call returns successfully.
providers.rederivation: UNSUPPORTED: no deterministic provider-native derived reconstruction primitive is exposed.
providers.restart: Construct a new client over the same persistent Qdrant and SQLite history state; do not clear the namespace.

providers.architecture_role: explicit source, observation, and derived-state negative control
providers.name: Hindsight
providers.quiescence: Poll the returned provider operation until completed; failed is ERROR and submitted/processing is not quiescent.
providers.rederivation: POST native consolidation and poll its explicit operation status to completed.
providers.restart: Restart the run-owned service/client over the same persistent PostgreSQL/pgvector state; do not reset the bank.

providers.architecture_role: session/archive, asynchronous extraction, memory_diff, and one-to-many derived memory URIs
providers.name: OpenViking
providers.quiescence: Poll the provider task until status equals completed; failure is ERROR and fixed sleep is never completion evidence.
providers.rederivation: Invoke the provider-native session extraction endpoint and require its task to complete.
providers.restart: Restart the run-owned service over the same persistent workspace, vector index, archive, task, and cache state; do not reset the namespace.

research_questions.RQ1: Across heterogeneous memory providers, how reliably do supersession, revocation/invalidation, deletion, and restart/reconstruction converge to the intended authoritative state across source and derived memory surfaces?
research_questions.RQ2: When a lifecycle transition fails to eliminate operational influence, which memory surface or propagation edge causes the residual or resurrected state, and under what reconstruction or re-derivation event does it become visible?
research_questions.RQ3: For lifecycle failures exposing the same unauthorized context, how much does downstream LLM choice change stale-memory-driven unsafe-decision probability? RQ3 is subordinate and runs only on frozen residual contexts.
research_questions.RQ4: Can a provider-independent pre-LLM mediator enforce current authority over retrieved source and derived records using lifecycle status plus provenance/lineage while preserving history for audit?

residual_advancement_rule: provider-correlated non-authoritative derived state remains retrievable
descendants of deleted or revoked state remain visible
state disappears and then reappears after restart
state disappears and then reappears after re-derivation
source and derived surfaces disagree about current authority
the three frozen repetitions disagree about normalized authority exposure
rq3_advancement_rule: the exact pre-LLM delivered context can be frozen
the authority of delivered context is known sufficiently for defense evaluation
the context reaches the model boundary

run_order.rationale: Deterministic ordering improves reproducibility and simplifies state and cleanup auditing.

scenarios.name: HARD_DELETE_RESTART
steps: restart or reconstruct over the same persistent state

scenarios.name: HARD_DELETE_REDERIVE
steps: write and create observable derived state
invoke a real provider-native re-derivation trigger

status_definitions.ABSENT: A valid exact retrieval contains neither expected current nor stale exact text.
status_definitions.BLOCKED: Experiment infrastructure or runtime prevented execution.
status_definitions.ERROR: A provider or harness operation unexpectedly failed.
status_definitions.INCONSISTENT: The three repetitions disagree at aggregation level; all raw runs remain authoritative evidence.
status_definitions.UNKNOWN_PROVENANCE: A visible provider record cannot be attributed through direct evidence.
status_definitions.UNSUPPORTED: The provider lacks the required native capability; no substitute operation is emulated.
